extracted.intended_audience: members of the London Mathematical Society; research mathematicians, postgraduate students and other mathematicians interested in meetings, publications, prizes, jobs and society business
extracted.subtask_description: Monthly London Mathematical Society newsletter containing meeting and conference announcements, prize and publication submission rules, subscription and pricing policies, job adverts, and instructions for applications and bookings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Election of Council and Officers (AGM procedures)
rubrics_metrics.description: The election of Council and Officers is governed by Article 9 of the Charter, by Articles 18, 24 and 31 of the Statutes, and by By-Law I of the By-Laws of the Society.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By-Law I was amended (June meeting) to allow the ballot to be held under the Single Transferable Vote system; nominations for vacancies on Council will arise from the Nominating Committee rather than from Council itself. Ballot papers will not be circulated with the October Newsletter but sent in a special mailing in October including details of the voting procedure and information about the candidates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Dinner booking and payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Booking for the Annual Dinner must be returned together with the payment form to the LMS office by the stated deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 1999 Annual Dinner: held after the AGM on 19 November; cost £26.25 per person; members may book places for guests. The booking/payment form enclosed with the Newsletter should be returned to the LMS office by Monday 15 November (or by the date specified for the year).

rubrics_metrics.name: JCM (LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics) subscription access and conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Subscriptions to the electronic LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics provide access to the full archive for a specified calendar year; access is by username and password assigned to the individual subscriber.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until end of 1999 subscriptions are free; to get access for calendar year 2000 complete the membership subscription form. Payment provides access to the full archive (Volumes 1–3 in 2000) for one calendar year (1 January–31 December). After registration there is ~10 days' delay before electronic access goes live. The username/password will be sent by e-mail; only the individual subscriber may use them (personal-use condition). Index and abstracts remain freely available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual subscription renewal and payment methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Members must complete and return the renewal form with remittance unless already paying by Direct Debit and not changing publications; Direct Debit is the preferred payment method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual subscription due 1 November. If paying by Direct Debit and not changing publications, no action required. If changing publications, fully complete and return the form. Members paying by Direct Debit will be debited on 17 January 2000. Other members should enclose a cheque (sterling or US$) or request a Direct Debit mandate if they have a UK bank account. Credit card facility is available but Direct Debit is preferred. If renewal form missing, contact Society office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publications pricing policy — personal-use restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: Discounted prices for LMS journals are intended for personal use only; journals bought at discounted member prices must be kept among personal belongings and not deposited in libraries or public areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should not be deposited, even temporarily, in a library, common room or other public area. Issues should be accessible to other mathematicians or students only with your permission given individually in each instance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meeting/Conference travel support application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for partial financial support to attend LMS meetings or conferences should be addressed to the Meetings and Membership Secretary and must include an estimate of expenses and a very brief curriculum vitae.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research students should include brief letters of endorsement/endorsement from their supervisors. Send requests to Meetings and Membership Secretary, De Morgan House, and include the estimate of expenses and CV; follow any additional application instructions in the meeting announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize — scope and eligible monograph
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize is awarded for a mathematical monograph of an expository nature presenting the latest developments in an active research area in which the applicant has made important contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The monograph should be expository and present recent developments; the applicant is expected to have made important contributions to the area covered by the monograph.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize — language and length requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The monograph must be original, written in English, and of at least 150 pages; in exceptional cases manuscripts in other languages may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are asked to submit English-language works where possible; exceptional non-English manuscripts may be considered but preference stated for English and minimum length is 150 pages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize — prize, publication and acceptance conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The prize amounts to €10,000; the winning monograph will be published in Birkhäuser’s Progress in Mathematics series subject to normal copyright/author-rights regulations. Submission implies acceptance of all stated conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submission of a monograph means the author accepts the prize conditions (publication arrangements, copyright regulations). The name of the prize-winner will be announced (e.g., in Barcelona in April 2000).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ferran Sunyer i Balaguer Prize — submission format and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Monographs should preferably be typeset in TeX; authors should send, before the deadline, a hard copy and two disks with the DVI and PS files together with an accompanying letter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the 1999/2000 competition authors should send hard copy + two disks containing DVI and PostScript files plus an accompanying letter to the Foundation address by 5 December 1999 (or the deadline given). Prefer TeX typesetting to ease production if selected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility and application criteria for certain summer schools
rubrics_metrics.description: Summer schools (e.g., Geometry of quiver-representations, Homological conjectures) are aimed at young researchers (i.e., aged under 35) from the EU and associated countries, with applications possible for full support for travel and local expenses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The TMR programme particularly encourages applicants from less-favoured regions; applicants should consult the organisers or coordinator for application forms and details, and may apply for travel/local support where offered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newton Institute conference (Non-Fermi Liquid Effects) — application, poster and participation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications to attend must be submitted by the stated closing date; poster offers with title and short (<10 lines) abstract should be sent by the poster deadline; participation is limited (~80 participants) and limited financial support may be available for young researchers from EC countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference package costs (example: £260) include registration, accommodation for specified nights and meals; application forms available on WWW and should be sent to the named contact. Poster offers limited in number; send title + short abstract by the stated deadline (e.g., 30 October 1999).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conference/Workshop contribution selection and fees (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific committees reserve the right to select contributions for presentation; participation fees, registration procedures, lodging and abstract submission details will be distributed in subsequent announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: International Congress on Differential Geometry — participation fee announced (e.g., US$100 or 15,000 pesetas), scientific committee reserves right to select contributions for oral presentation; further details (registration, abstracts, programme) to be distributed in a later announcement and via website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theodore von Kármán Prize — award criteria and eligibility period
rubrics_metrics.description: The von Kármán Prize is awarded every five years for a notable application of mathematics to mechanics and/or the engineering sciences, made during the five to ten years preceding the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award may be for a single notable achievement or for a collection of achievements; selection committee members named for transparency; prize aims at notable applications made in the recent (5–10 year) past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Academic job application requirements (Lectureships)
rubrics_metrics.description: Candidates for lectureships should demonstrate a strong commitment to high-quality teaching and an excellent research record or outstanding research potential; applications should include a CV, publications list and names of referees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific posts may state research-area preferences (e.g., analysis, algebra, differential geometry, logic). Salary scale and start date are given; informal enquiries directed to named contact(s). Closing dates specified (e.g., 8 or 29 October 1999).

rubrics_metrics.name: Student-only sale restriction for certain software/editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Sale of specific student editions (e.g., Mathcad 8 Student Version) is restricted to students at educational institutions; valid student identification is required for purchase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vendors require proof of student status at point of sale; network or other licensing terms may be separately specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: LMS Journal of Computation and Mathematics — editorial scope and publication policies
rubrics_metrics.description: The LMSJCM is an all-electronic refereed journal with the same standards as other LMS journals; it is a journal of record committed to indefinite archiving and does not claim copyright from its authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The journal allows updates and discussions to be added while preserving the main text; ensures rapid publication after acceptance in high-quality PDF, provides hyperlinks for cross-references. Papers invited in categories: mathematics that benefit from being electronic for format reasons; computational aspects of mathematics; mathematical aspects of computation. Enquiries to the Executive Editor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poster/abstract length guideline (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Poster offers should include title and a short abstract of less than a specified line limit (e.g., <10 lines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the Newton Institute conference, offers of posters (numbers limited) should include title and a short (<10 lines) abstract and be sent to the named organiser by the given deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsletter submission deadline for items and advertisements
rubrics_metrics.description: Items and advertisements for inclusion in the Newsletter should be sent to the Editor to arrive before the first day of the month prior to publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Newsletter is published monthly except in August. Send items/advertisements by e-mail, fax or post and observe the copy deadline to ensure inclusion in the desired issue.
